## 1. Executive Summary & Epistemic Synthesis

Cosmogenesis has transitioned over the past six decades from qualitative metaphysical extrapolation to an empirical discipline governed by high-precision astrophysics. The standard Hot Big Bang framework is supported by five independent observational pillars: the blackbody spectrum of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), light-element synthesis via Standard Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (SBBN), spacetime metric expansion and cosmic time dilation, the acoustic sound horizon ruler, and the scale-dependent primordial tilt.

However, standard cosmological theory (flat $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ coupled with the Standard Model of particle physics) is an **effective infrared approximation**. It fails fundamentally at both ultraviolet (initial singularity, inflation mechanics, Sakharov baryogenesis) and infrared (cosmological constant vacuum energy, Hubble tension, dark matter identity) horizons. Below is the definitive empirical assessment of what is known, what remains unexplained, and the concrete observational pathways required to resolve each open problem.
